summary: The Engineer is a pet + tradeskill profession, and its implant set is built around one hard constraint the other classes do not have: EVERY robot summon requires Matter Creation AND Time & Space at (near) the SAME value, and both clusters have the SAME three homes - Head shiny, Right Hand bright, Eye faded. So you cannot 'max MC' the way an MP does; you must SPLIT them - Shiny Matter Creation in the Head, Bright Time & Space in the Right Hand and Faded Time & Space in the Eye - because a Shiny bonus equals a Bright plus a Faded of the same QL, which lands MC and TS on the same number. Around that go Matter Metamorphosis (the aura/shield lines and the pet buffs), Biological Metamorphosis (pet heals), Nano C. Init, Nano Pool / Max Nano, and Pistol - the Engineer's cheapest weapon skill (IP cost 1.5) and the only profession whose core weapon cluster sits in an otherwise-dead slot (Right Wrist shiny). The TRADESKILL build below is a genuinely separate, swap-in second set: the Engineer is the game's crafting profession (Mech Eng, Elec Eng, Quantum FT, Weapon Smithing, Pharma Tech, Chemistry, Nano Programming, Computer Literacy, Break & Entry are all cheap for it) and those clusters collide even harder than MC/TS do. Every placement below was validated against reference/implants.json - each cluster is only ever put in a slot/grade its cluster list actually allows, and no cluster is used twice at the same grade.
_gradeMeaning: shiny = biggest bonus, bright = ~60%, faded = ~40%. A skill placed in two implants (e.g. one bright + one faded) stacks. Because each cluster has exactly one shiny/bright/faded home, some skills can only be obtained at a lower grade once their shiny home slot is used for something else.
_qualityNote: QL values are the typical top-tier target for regular implants (~200). Higher QLs exist via twinking/laddering and Jobe/refined clusters; at true endgame several slots are usually replaced by symbiants (see engineer-symbiants.json). QLs here are guidance, not sourced exact values.

clusterCollisions: Matter Creation and Time & Space have IDENTICAL homes (shiny Head, bright Right Hand, faded Eye). Only three slots exist for two skills the Engineer must keep equal - hence the shiny/bright+faded split. This collision is unique to the Engineer among pet classes: an MP leans on one school, a Crat/Engi cannot.
Matter Metamorphosis and Biological Metamorphosis both want Chest bright. MM wins (Engineer MM requirements reach 1769; BM only 836), so BM is left with its Waist-faded home only.

Seven tradeskills (Mech Eng, Quantum FT, Pharma Tech, Chemistry, Nano Programming, Computer Literacy, Treatment) all share Head shiny / Eye bright / Right Hand faded. Three homes, seven claimants - the tradeskill build can implant at most three of them meaningfully, which is exactly why the Engineer also stacks tradeskill GEAR and the +200 composite buff.

Electrical Engineering (Eye shiny + Head bright), Weapon Smithing (Right Hand shiny + Eye faded) and Break & Entry (Right Arm shiny + Left Arm bright) sit OUTSIDE that pile-up, so they are always worth taking - even on the combat build.
ladder: Max Treatment every level (needed to equip each QL of implant: Treatment req = trunc(4.723717064*QL + 6.767295257) ~ QL*4.7+11; governing ability req = QL*2+4 - so a QL200 implant needs ~947 Treatment and ~404 of its ability). Treatment is cheap for an Engineer (IP cost 1.6, vs 2.0 for an MP). To reach top QL, ladder up: equip the survivability/Treatment implants first, stack Treatment- and ability-buffs (Trader wrangles, First-Aid/Bio-Met stims, Expertise/Essence, Behemoth/Sadist), then swap in the high-QL implants one QL step at a time. The Engineer builds its OWN clusters: Nano Programming to assemble a cluster is 2.0*mult*QL (shiny), 1.5*mult*QL (bright), 1.0*mult*QL (faded), and NP is a 1.2-cost skill for an Engineer - so unlike most classes it can self-supply the whole set. Use AOLadderer / Nano Nanny / the Auno Implant Designer to solve the exact ladder for your character (AO-Universe's Engineer guide recommends Nano Nanny specifically).
_deviations: AO-Universe's Engineer Guide MKIII and aodb's Engineer Guide both specify only the PRINCIPLE (shiny MC + bright/faded TS, plus Intelligence, Matter Met, Max Health as 'essential', Bio Met / weapon skill / Run Speed as 'recommended') and then point at Nano Nanny rather than publishing a full slot table. The aodb sample table it does show is a LOW-LEVEL Agility/Stamina-gated set (Head shiny Time & Space, Eye faded Matter Creation, Chest shiny Max Health, Right Arm shiny Strength, Legs shiny Agility, Waist shiny Fire AC, Feet shiny Evade). The 13-slot tables above are my mapping-consistent endgame extension of that principle, not a copied guide layout.

The aodb sample puts Time & Space in Head shiny and Matter Creation in Eye faded (the mirror of my split). Either orientation is correct - what matters is that one school gets the shiny and the other gets bright+faded. I chose MC-shiny because the Engineer's single highest MC requirement in the local nano data (2047, Improved Isochronal Sloughing Combat Field id 273343) is marginally above its highest TS requirement.

The aodb sample spends Right Arm shiny on Strength and Legs/Waist on raw Agility/Stamina/Max Health. That is a level-sub-100 twinking set; at 200+ those slots are better spent on Break & Entry, the evades and Body Dev., which is what is written above.

Neither guide publishes a tradeskill implant table ('the guide doesn't provide a dedicated trade-skill implant template'). The tradeskill build above is derived entirely from reference/implants.json (which cluster is legal where) plus the Engineer cost factors in reference/skillcaps.json - it is a derivation, not a quoted build.
Run Speed is listed as 'recommended' by both guides but has NO implant cluster at any slot/grade in reference/implants.json - it is a gear/nano skill only. Not included, deliberately.
_verification: Every (slot, grade, cluster) triple in both builds was checked against reference/implants.json slots[].shiny/bright/faded - no cluster is placed in a slot that does not list it.
The cluster invariant was checked per build: within each of the two 13-slot builds, no cluster name appears twice at the same grade.

Nano-skill thresholds quoted in the notes were read from engineer-nanos.json (generated from the local nanos.ocp): Ravening M-60 id 275815 MC>1959 / TS>1957; Improved Isochronal Sloughing Combat Field id 273343 MC>2047 / TS>2047; Intrusive Aura of Slave id 275835 MM>1769; Sympathetic Fortress Screen id 154562 MM>870; A Maker's Touch id 116791 BM>760; Master's Repairs id 270351 BM>836; Engineer Composite Specialist Tradeskills id 273346 PM>1033 / SI>1033.

Engineer IP cost factors quoted (Pistol 1.5, Grenade 2.0, MechE/ElecE/QFT/WS/Tutoring 1.0, Chemistry/NanoProgramming 1.2, CompLit 1.3, Treatment/TrapDisarm/B&E/NanoCInit 1.6, NanoPool 1.8, BM/PM/SI 2.4, Evade-ClsC 4.0) come from reference/skillcaps.json, Engineer column (index 5 of _professionOrder).

Weapon-skill choice (Pistol primary, Grenade secondary) and the pistol special list (AimedShot / Burst / FlingShot / FullAuto) were taken from the already-generated engineer-weapons.json, which was present when this file was written - NOT inferred from skillcaps alone. skillcaps.json agrees (Pistol 1.5 is the Engineer's cheapest weapon skill).
_unverified: Exact QLs: no located guide publishes an endgame Engineer implant QL sheet. The ~QL200 target is the standard top-of-the-line regular-implant figure, not a sourced number for this profession.

The Head-shiny choice on the tradeskill build (Nano Programming vs Computer Literacy vs Mechanical Engineering) is a judgement call from the cost factors and the collision analysis; no guide publishes a ranked Engineer tradeskill implant priority.

Which of Chemistry / Pharma Tech / Computer Literacy is the better pick for the single Right-Hand-faded slot depends on what you actually build (Chemistry for nanos/stims, Pharma Tech for medical, Computer Literacy for NCU/alien tech). Quantum FT was chosen as the default because it is a 1.0-cost Engineer skill with no other home; this is a preference, not a sourced recommendation.

At endgame Engineers commonly replace several implant slots with Control-unit symbiants; that tradeoff is covered qualitatively here and in detail in engineer-symbiants.json, but the combined implant+symbiant optimum is not modelled.

The '(filler)' picks (Head faded Tutoring, Ear shiny Perception, Ear bright Psychology, Right Arm bright Physic. Init, Left Arm shiny Brawling, Left Wrist bright/faded, Left Hand shiny Fast Attack, Waist shiny Cold AC) are my choice of the least-useless cluster each list offers; no source ranks them.
